issue.title: 4.9: Domain-exclusion regex hardening
issue.body_excerpt: Cap length and escape user patterns.

affected_files.role: primary - matchesDomainPattern() (line ~12) builds a regex from user input with two transformations: `.replace(/\./g, '\\.')` (escape dots) and `.replace(/\*/g, '.*')` (wildcard). A pathological pattern like '*' alone or 'a*b*c*d*...' compiles a regex with unbounded .* chains that can cause exponential backtracking against certain inputs. Also no length cap on the pattern. Fix: (a) cap pattern length (e.g. 256 chars) and return false on overflow, (b) use `RegExp.escape` if available (Node 24+, baseline 2024) or escape ALL regex metacharacters before splicing, (c) limit the number of `*` segments (e.g. 8).
secondary - add a test case that feeds a pathological pattern ('*' * 1000 or 'a*b*c*d*...') and asserts the call returns false quickly. Add a test for the length cap and the metacharacter escape.

analysis.current_implementation: src/content/domain-utils.js:17-21: `const regexPattern = normalizedPattern.replace(/\./g, '\\.').replace(/\*/g, '.*'); const regex = new RegExp(`^${regexPattern}$`);` — accepts arbitrary user input, only escapes dots, only converts `*`. A user can add a pattern like '***' (compiles to .*.*.* — exponential backtracking risk), or a pattern with 1000 characters of 'a' followed by '*' (linear but unbounded memory). There is no length cap.
analysis.limitations: Patterns come from the user's own Settings → Excluded Domains list, so the trust model is 'user trusting themselves' — but the regex compilation runs in the service worker / content script on every page load, and a user can be tricked into pasting a hostile pattern (a malicious FAQ, a support-ticket suggestion, etc.). The hard cap should be at the input layer (the settings sheet) AND at the matcher (defense in depth).
analysis.change_surface: 1-2 files. domain-utils.js: add input validation at the top of matchesDomainPattern — (a) reject patterns longer than 256 chars, (b) reject patterns with more than 8 `*` segments, (c) escape ALL regex metacharacters (the current code only escapes `.`). The cleanest approach: replace the manual replace-chain with a `escapeRegex(s)` helper that escapes the standard 12 metacharacters, then only convert `*` AFTER escaping. The test file gets 2-3 new cases.
analysis.root_cause: User-supplied patterns flow into `new RegExp()` with only minimal escaping (dots) and no length / count / metacharacter limits. A pathological pattern can compile a regex that backtracks pathologically on common inputs (ReDoS) or simply wastes memory.

options.name: Harden matchesDomainPattern with cap + full escape
options.summary: In src/content/domain-utils.js, rewrite matchesDomainPattern: (1) `if (pattern.length > 256) return false;` (2) `if ((pattern.match(/\*/g) || []).length > 8) return false;` (3) replace the manual `.replace(/\./g, ...)` with a proper escape helper that handles all 12 regex metacharacters, then convert `*` to `.*` AFTER escaping. Add a guard so a pattern equal to the exact domain still matches (the early return at line 15 already handles this). Add tests for: length cap, asterisk count cap, and a pathological 'a*a*a*a*a*b' pattern against 'aaaaaaaaaaaaaaab' (linear backtracking case).
pros: Caps ReDoS risk and metacharacter injection in one pass
Backward compatible for normal patterns (dots, stars, subdomains)
cons: Existing tests must still pass — verify with `npm run test:run tests/unit/domain-patterns.test.js`
options.risk_details: Verify: `npm run test:run tests/unit/domain-patterns.test.js` passes, plus a new test for the pathological case. The acceptance 'Pathological `*` patterns cannot compile unbounded `.*` chains' is met by the asterisk count cap.
